title: Will there be more than 170 transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Nov 2, 2026 to Nov 8, 2026? Above 170
rules: If the number of transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 170 from Nov 2, 2026 to Nov 8, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: The total is calculated by summing daily counts from Nov 2, 2026 to Nov 8, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

blind.reasoning: IMF PortWatch weekly Bab el-Mandeb totals have recently been about 180-200 (around 26-29 ships a day), and even the lowest monthly average in the past two years (27 a day, September 2026) works out to about 189 a week. The threshold of 170 needs only about 24.3 ships a day, so a normal week clears it. The main risks are a new Houthi escalation now that they control Yemen's Red Sea coast, normal weekly swings, and data revisions.
blind.falsifier: A new Houthi attack campaign or major incident near Bab el-Mandeb in late October or early November 2026 that pushes daily PortWatch transits below about 24 a day for the Nov 2-8 week.

final.reasoning: Recent PortWatch weeks of about 182-202 sit comfortably above 170, so the market's 0.865 is plausible. My estimate leans slightly lower because of Houthi escalation risk and data revisions, but the roughly 3-point edge is too small to act on.
